title: Quantized cross-encoder matrix fusion rollout policy and smoke-suite
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Introduce a controlled rollout policy for a quantized multilingual cross-encoder variant that fuses a narrow dense matrix optimization ("matrix-fusion") with adaptive KV warmstart. The goal is to reduce per-request token-cost and P95 latency on rerank endpoints while preserving or improving nDCG/Recall across English + four target locales (es, fr, de, ja). This ticket covers policy definition, smoke/eval suite, monitoring dashboards, and canary gating thresholds for progressive rollout.
acceptance_criteria: Canary traffic run for 48 hours with at least 100k rerank requests and no stability regressions
Quality regression: aggregated nDCG@10 drop <= 0.6% across evaluation testsets per locale
Latency SLAs: P95 inference latency for 128-token pairwise rerank <= 120ms on dedicated GPU pool; no >5% tail spikes during canary
Cost: per-1k-token token-cost reduction >= 18% relative to baseline cross-encoder v1.3 quantized baseline
Automated smoke suite executed on each canary step and passes (functional + perf + locale sanity checks)
Rollback path documented and validated (automatic and manual)
tasks: Build quantized matrix-fusion binary and package variant tag: crossenc-qmf-1.0
Add inference config flags for KV warmstart TTL and adaptive warmstart policy
Author smoke/eval harness: per-locale nDCG/Recall calculation and latency instrumentation
Create canary routing policy in Smart Router with staged traffic: 0.5% -> 2% -> 10% -> 50%
Instrument dashboards: per-route model-level nDCG, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, cost per 1k tokens
Write regression gating logic: block rollout if throughput or nDCG thresholds fail
Prepare rollback automation and documentation for on-call runbooks
Run internal perf benchmarking and collect kernel-level traces for root-cause analysis

metrics: P50/P95/P99 latency (ms) for pairwise rerank 32/64/128 token pairs
KV cache hit rate and median warmstart time
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Internal lab validation - run Jupyter evaluation on full dev sets, perf microbenchmarks (done)
Stage 1: Canary 0.5% traffic for 6 hours (smoke + perf) - automatic rollback if p95 > 130ms or nDCG drop > 1.0% on any locale
Stage 2: Canary 2% traffic for 24 hours - run full nightly eval and check long-tail slices; require de < 0.6% nDCG drop
Stage 3: Canary 10% traffic for 48 hours - monitor cost and tail latencies; escalate to on-call if error-rate increases >0.2% absolute
Stage 4: Ramp to 50% then 100% with 72h soak at each step, only if all metrics stable and regression gates passed
Rollback: immediate automatic rollback to crossenc-v1.3 if any gate violated in a stage; manual rollback path documented for partial degradations
risks: Quantization causes locale-specific quality regressions for long-tail tokens (observed in de)
Matrix-fusion kernel selection may increase tail latency under certain sequence-length distributions
Adaptive KV warmstart misconfiguration could increase memory churn and evictions, reducing throughput
Dashboards may not surface subtle per-slice regressions without the expanded evaluation harness
